HROMBIN-ACTIVATED platelets express @
hemagglutination activity (enhanced lectin ac-
tivity) not expressed by nonactivated platelets, and
this agglutinin mediates the direct platelet-platelet
interactions that cause the aggregation of thrombin-
activated platelets. The enhanced agglutinin activity
‘of thrombin-activated platelets is composed of two
‘components: a plasma membrane-bound component
‘and a soluble component.” The expression of both
forms of the agglutinin activity is dependent on
secretion."* Accordingly, washed platelets exposed to
fibrinogen and adenosine diphosphate (ADP) in
‘Tyrode buffer, in the absence of stirring, lack
enhanced hemagglutination activity (unpublished
data). The soluble, but not the membrane-bound,
agglutinin activity is dependent on fibrin formation.’
‘The function of both forms of the agglutinin activity is
inhibited by the same compounds that inhibit the
aggregation of thrombin-activated platelets."? In this.
article, platelets from individuals with congenital
bleeding disorders that have selective effects were
studied in an attempt {0 correlate their associated,
platelet agglutinin deficiencies, if any, with their
abnormal behavior in aggregation. We describe the
platelet-bound and platelet-free (soluble) agglutinin
activities of activated washed platelets from patients
with the bleeding disorders, congenital afibrinogen-
emia,‘ Glanzmann’s thrombasthenia, gray platelet
syndrome,’ and Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome.*
